method: Sayari MCP: search_entities (entity resolution by name + identifiers), find_beneficial_owners (compact, upstream ownership; top results only), check_watchlist (max_depth 1 = direct links only unless noted; limit 2-3), risk_levels taken from the search row or get_entity_summary of the selected entity. Tradeverifyd MCP: search_entities -> entity_score -> annotation_count (search) / entity_annotations. All findings are tool outputs recorded verbatim-ish; they are data-provider signals, not allegations. 'No hits returned' means only that the call returned nothing at the depth/limit used. game.* fields are ASSUMED calibration, not data.

notes: 1) Traps: PT Huayue Nickel Cobalt and Congo Dongfang International Mining are the clear traps (Sayari ownership records point to China-tagged owners; Huayue also carries sub-tier forced-labour flags). MP Materials and Teck are 'partial' cases: Sayari returns a China-linked holder (Shenghe; Fullbloom/CIC) but no stake size or date, so the game should treat these as minority/possibly historical stakes rather than control. 2) Tradeverifyd scores sit in a narrow 700-745 band, all level 'Low', and every entity returned annotation_count 0 (entity_annotations for Huayue also returned 0 records); the score does not separate traps from clean names, so the game should lean on Sayari flags for its warning signals. 3) Watchlist hits are network/trade-record links (ships_to / receives_from), not direct listings of the company itself; Sayari 'psa_' and '_adjacent' risk factors describe proximity, not wrongdoing. 4) Several Sayari and Tradeverifyd nodes are conflated (USAC aliases; Umicore node titled 'Ultra Move'; two Teck nodes with different owner data); verify before showing on screen. 5) country-level flags basel_aml / cpi_score appear on nearly every entity and are omitted from game flags. 6) All game.* values (upfront $M, docPerQ, lag quarters) are assumptions keyed to production status, not tool outputs.
